dasārahā.notes: SN 20.7 names the Dasārahas as the owners of the Ānaka drum. SN 20.6 shares the cited page and gives the simile of the four archers.

daṇḍakappaka.notes: AN 6.62 names the Kosalan town, places Ānanda at the Aciravatī and records the question about Devadatta. The app titles this discourse Purisindriyañāṇasutta. DPPN calls it Udānasutta. AN 6.61 is set at Isipatana near Varanasi.

devadaha.notes: MN 101, SN 22.2 and SN 35.134 each name Devadaha as a Sakyan town. DPPN’s abbreviated reference iv.124f points to SN 35.134, which is missing from the citation list. SN 22.1 is set in the Bhagga country. The packet also misses Devadahaṁ at MN 110:26.1, where the chapter’s closing list names MN 101.

devadatta.notes: MN 29 names Devadatta after his departure, and SN 17.31 explicitly attributes the schism to him. Check DPPN’s account of Ud 1.5 against the edition it used. The app’s Pāli at Ud 1.5:1.3 lists ten elders and omits Devadatta. In MN 58:3.13–15 the words that anger him are the prediction of his rebirth in hell. Candikāputta reports Devadatta’s teaching in AN 9.26. AN 9.25 shares the cited page. The hits in AN 4.70, AN 8.10 and SN 6.15 occur only in closing lists of discourse titles.

devahita.notes: SN 7.13 names the brahmin who supplies Upavāṇa with hot water and molasses. SN 7.12 concerns Udaya. At AN 8.38:5.3 devahito means ‘good for the gods’, but the tap offers only the personal name. SN 7.22:4.1 names Devahita in the chapter’s closing list. The packet misses the Pāli story heading at Dhp 423:0, where Devahitabrāhmaṇavatthu shows the Devahita line when tapped.
